data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Erde was the goddess of the earth. She represented fertility, nurturing, and stability. Her name is derived from the Greek word for 'earth'. The name Erde carries the meaning “Earth Goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Erde usually hope their child will grow to embody earth goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Erde belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Earth Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Erde total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name Erde holds significant cultural influence as it is “rooted” in ancient Greek mythology. Erde is a nod to the goddess of the earth and reminds us of the importance of our planet and the natural world. The name also carries connotations of growth, fertility, and sustainability that may inspire individuals to appreciate and care for the earth.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Erde holds deep spiritual significance as it honors the divine feminine and the nurturing power of the earth. The goddess Erde embodies the spirit of creation and renewal, and her name can serve as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things and the power of the natural world to sustain and heal. For Christians, the name Erde may also carry symbolism related to the central idea of creation and nurturing found in Christian theology.
